decisions.summary: There is no package.json, src/, or any TypeScript/TSX in this repository; 'convert' can only apply to the harness documents and/or mean building a new Vite reference implementation. The plan does not assume either until OQ-1 is answered.

All framework-independent content (non-negotiable rules, token system, palette presets, pattern language, copy rules, cat gag, interactive shell) is preserved verbatim in any conversion; only the mechanism-level references (fonts, metadata, data fetching, routing, 404, build commands, deploy target) change.

Recommended default if the user does not care: Vite + React + TypeScript with @tailwindcss/vite, React Router (SPA), @fontsource IBM Plex Mono/Sans for fonts, import.meta.glob + react-markdown for markdown posts, client-side GitHub fetch for live ticker stats (rendered only on success), static index.html meta + theme-color, catch-all '*' route for the 404. Pending OQ-2 confirmation.

openQuestions.question: This repo has no app code — only the design harness (AGENTS.md, README.md, prompt). What should 'convert to Vite' produce? (a) Retarget the harness docs so agents generate a Vite app instead of Next.js (recommended, smallest change, matches the repo's 'harness-first' status); (b) build the reference implementation now, on Vite, using the 'Test User' identity from `prompt`; or (c) both.

Which Vite flavour? (a) Vite + React + React Router SPA (simplest; no SSR/SSG, blog pages not pre-rendered for SEO); (b) Vike (vite-plugin-ssr) with pre-rendering so the blog/OG metadata stay server-rendered like Next.js; (c) TanStack Start. Default if unanswered: (a).
Should the README's deploy target stay Vercel (works for Vite static output) or change to a generic 'any static host' instruction?

routing.reason: No new visual or UX design question: the design system, tokens and pattern language are unchanged. This is a build-tool/framework retarget. Routing to design would only be warranted if the user chose SSR-less SPA and wanted the blog/OG behaviour redesigned, which is not a visual question.
